lede: What to do each day, each week, each month and each quarter from October to July, with dated steps so both final pieces (the 60-minute specialized talk and the three-session Sahṛdaya offering) are built gradually instead of in July.

items: **Sit with the ajapā-haṃsa** for the length you set at your practice baseline. Add attention, not effort.
**Log it** in your practice log: date, length, and one line on what you noticed. Your mentor reviews the log in every one-to-one.
**Read a little** of the month's required book. About 30 minutes on most days finishes a book a month.
**Notice task language** in your own teaching: any phrase that asks a student to produce what they already have.
**Reading**: roughly a quarter of the month's book, with notes for your reflection.
**Project notebook**: ten minutes on one line for the talk and one for the offering (more below).

**Field hours**: alternate weeks between observing a senior teacher (with notes against the six competencies) and practice-teaching. About 30 minutes a week of each keeps you on pace for ten hours of each.
**Book Club**: join or propose one when the cohort is reading the same chapters. Any mentee can propose a session.
**Immersion weekend** (October to May): Open Session and Practicum, 2.5 hours each, both halves live. Attendance must stay at 80% or above.
**One-to-one** with Jacob or Nataraj Chaitanya, 45 minutes, with a booking summary sent ahead.
**Articulation session** with your partner, about an hour: each of you explains one teaching from the month through an analogy or image a new student could hold. Log the image you used.
**Written reflection** on the required book (about 30 minutes), posted to the cohort group by the last day of the month.
**That month's project steps**, listed on each month card below.

**End of November (Q1)**: read back through your practice log; rate yourself on the six competencies; check field hours (aim for about 3 of observation and 3 of practice-teaching); bring your talk longlist and Session 1 angles.
**End of March (mid-year)**: same review, plus attendance check. Aim for about 6 and 6 hours. Talk topic agreed, Session 1 written, ST 7.59 memorised.
**End of June (readiness)**: observation and practice-teaching complete at 10 and 10. Talk recorded in full, upadeśa led for peers, delivery dates booked, final report outlined.
**Retreat practicum**, in person or the facilitated online version.
**The 60-minute specialized talk**, live and recorded, assessed by a mentor. One revision is allowed.
**The three-session offering** to a real group, recorded, with you leading the haṃsa-upadeśa in Session 2 and your mentor assessing it.
**Final report** (positionality, lineage, how SLBT moved into your teaching) and the **competency check** (open book, terminology and framework).

week.title: Week 1 · Open
items: Start the new book.
Book your one-to-one and send your summary.
Fix a date with your articulation partner (new partner in Oct, Dec, Feb, Apr, Jun).
Check this month's project steps.

week.title: Week 2 · Practise
items: Reading, second quarter.
Observation hour, with notes against the competencies.
Articulation session: one teaching, one image each.

week.title: Week 3 · Teach
items: Reading, third quarter.
Practice-teaching hour. Record it if you can; you'll need student reports in May.
Work on this month's project step.
Propose or join a Book Club.

week.title: Week 4 · Gather
items: Finish the book.
Write and post your reflection.
Your one-to-one (last week of the month).
Log hours: observation, practice-teaching, articulation.
Notebook: one line for the talk, one for the offering.

steps.title: Start your project notebook
steps.detail: One page per month. After each immersion, reading and observation, note one possible talk theme and one possible Session 1 angle.
steps.evidence: Notebook started (show it at your December one-to-one)

steps.title: Longlist three possible talk topics
steps.detail: Three candidate topics for the 60-minute specialized talk, one sentence each, drawn from your notebook.
steps.evidence: Longlist brought to the Q1 review

steps.title: Note two or three Session 1 angles you could speak to
steps.detail: The angles come from the monthly books. Mark the ones you can speak to from your own life.

steps.title: Name your real group and venue
steps.detail: Who will you offer the three sessions to (your students, a studio, a community group), and where? Talk to the host now.
steps.evidence: Group and venue named in your January one-to-one

steps.title: Bring a talk topic proposal to your one-to-one
steps.detail: One paragraph: the topic, who it's for, and why you are the person to give it. Mentors confirm or redirect.
steps.evidence: Proposal in the one-to-one booking summary

steps.title: Choose your Session 1 angle
steps.detail: Pick one angle and its book. If you haven't read the book yet, schedule it.

steps.title: Memorise ST 7.59 in Sanskrit and English
steps.detail: "There is none who utters it, and none is found who checks it: the Haṃsa utters itself, abiding in the breast of living beings."

steps.title: Write the Session 1 talk
steps.detail: The whole talk, landing included, in under 1,500 words.

steps.title: Rehearse the Session 2 talk with your partner
steps.detail: Check every instruction against the use-and-avoid table in Part III of the manual. Rewrite any line that tasks a student with producing what they already have.

steps.title: Book your three dates and open sign-ups
steps.detail: Session 1, then Session 2 a week later, then Session 3 at least two weeks after Session 2. Latest possible start is Mon 5 Jul. Tell your mentor which Session 2 date they are assessing.
steps.evidence: Dates confirmed with venue and mentor

steps.title: Try a 10-minute seed version on your partner
steps.detail: Just the opening and the central image. You are testing whether the topic holds, not polishing.

steps.title: Practise paryavasāna responses on five recorded reports
steps.detail: Use five recorded student reports (from your practice-teaching, or provided by mentors). Carry each to its own conclusion without affirming, correcting or psychologising.

steps.title: Lead the full upadeśa for peers, under supervision
steps.detail: Arrange with your mentor. This comes before you offer it publicly.

steps.title: Bring the immersion 8 design to a full outline
steps.detail: The talk is designed at immersion 8. Turn that design into a full outline with sources, timings and the one practice you'll guide.

steps.title: Record a full 60-minute run-through
steps.detail: Deliver it to your partner or a small group, recorded. Watch it once before your one-to-one.

steps.title: Write the follow-on cohort plan
steps.detail: The 12 to 18 month practice cohort your new students join after Session 3: meeting rhythm, place, how people join.

steps.title: Mentor feedback on the run-through; book your delivery slot
steps.detail: Use your June one-to-one for the recording. Book a live delivery date in the first half of July.

steps.title: Draft the final report outline
steps.detail: Positionality, lineage, and how SLBT principles moved into your teaching.

steps.title: Deliver the 60-minute talk, live and recorded
steps.detail: Assessed by a mentor. It may be revised once, which is why it lands mid-month.

steps.title: Complete all three sessions with your group
steps.detail: Latest Session 3 date if you started on 5 Jul. Your mentor assesses the haṃsa-upadeśa you lead in Session 2.
steps.evidence: Recordings of all three sessions submitted

steps.title: Revised talk, if you're revising
steps.detail: The one permitted revision, delivered and recorded.

steps.title: Submit the final report and sit the competency check
steps.detail: The competency check is an open-book examination on terminology and framework.

spacing: Spacing rule for the offering: Session 2 comes one week after Session 1, and Session 3 at least two weeks after Session 2, so students arrive with real practice. Starting on Mon 5 Jul is the latest that finishes by the end of July; starting in June gives room for a missed week.

howTo: Book early in the month, with Jacob or Nataraj Chaitanya. Sessions run in the last week of the month.
When you book, send a short summary of what you want to work on. Send it at least two days before the session so your mentor can prepare.
Attach anything you want looked at: a draft, a recording, a page of your notebook.
Bring your practice log. It is reviewed every time.
template: What I want to work on:
One thing from my practice log:
Where I am on the talk:
Where I am on the offering:
oneToOne.note: Five lines is enough. Your mentor reads it before you meet.

footer: Drawn from the Sahṛdaya Upāya Training Manual (draft) and the 2026–27 articulation partner rotation. Pacing suggestions (reading time, weekly field hours, quarterly targets) are this schedule's own and can be adjusted.
